title: Phase out gas reservation and price caps in favour of more supply
action: Phase out Western Australia's domestic gas reservation and make the east-coast gas price cap temporary, focusing instead on bringing on new supply and pipeline capacity.
why: Reserving gas or capping its price diverts it from its most valuable use and weakens the price signals that draw new supply, which is what lowers prices in the long run.

evidence.source: Examining Barriers to More Efficient Gas Markets (Commission Research Paper)
evidence.quote: Policies that seek to counteract the pressures from structural adjustment arising from the opening of the export market, such as domestic gas reservation, could distort important signals for adjustment and are unlikely to be efficient or effective in the long run.

evidence.source: Examining Barriers to More Efficient Gas Markets (Commission Research Paper)
evidence.quote: Governments should be mindful that policies that interfere with market signals could undermine investment incentives, including incentives to bring on new sources of gas supply.

evidence.source: Examining Barriers to More Efficient Gas Markets (Commission Research Paper)
evidence.quote: The Commission's analysis and modelling indicate that a reservation policy would impose a cost on gas producers and ultimately on the broader community because it would divert the supply of gas from its highest value use

tradeoffs: Reservation and the cap were introduced to protect domestic users from export-linked price spikes; removing them works best alongside measures that add supply.
